title: JC H2 biology — cell: ultrastructure and biomolecules
subject: science

slots.label: Cell membrane
entries: Cell membrane: the fluid mosaic: a phospholipid bilayer with hydrophilic heads out and hydrophobic tails in, with channel proteins giving selective passage.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Nucleus
entries: Nucleus: the control centre: chromatin stores the instructions, nuclear pores let mRNA out, and the nucleolus makes ribosomal RNA.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Mitochondria
entries: Mitochondria: releasing energy from food: glucose and oxygen enter respiration on the cristae, whose folds multiply the surface area for ATP-making enzymes.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Chloroplast
entries: Chloroplast: capturing light energy: light drives into the grana for the light-dependent stage, while the stroma fixes carbon dioxide into sugar in the Calvin cycle.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: RER, SER and Golgi
entries: RER, SER and Golgi: the export line: ribosomes on the rough ER fold proteins, the smooth ER makes lipids, and the Golgi body packages and ships proteins in vesicles.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Tests for biomolecules
entries: Tests for biomolecules: four classics: Benedict's heated goes brick-red for reducing sugar, iodine blue-black for starch, Biuret purple for protein, and the emulsion test milky white for lipid.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Misconception
entries: Misconception: plant cells lack mitochondria: the claim fails because plant cells respire day and night, so a plant cell holds mitochondria alongside its chloroplasts.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Cell membrane
entries: A selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer with drifting proteins (the fluid mosaic): hydrophilic heads face water, hydrophobic tails face inward.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Nucleus
entries: The control centre storing DNA as chromatin, enclosed by a double nuclear envelope with pores for mRNA, and containing the nucleolus that makes ribosomal RNA.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Mitochondrion
entries: The site of aerobic respiration, with an inner membrane folded into cristae that give a large surface area for ATP-making enzymes.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Chloroplast
entries: The site of photosynthesis in plant cells: grana (thylakoid stacks) run the light-dependent stage and the stroma runs the Calvin cycle.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
entries: ER studded with ribosomes, where new proteins are folded.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
entries: ER without ribosomes, where lipids are made and substances are detoxified.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Golgi body
entries: A stack that modifies, packages and ships proteins out of the cell in vesicles.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Benedict's test
entries: The test for reducing sugar: add Benedict's solution and heat; blue to brick-red is positive.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Iodine test
entries: The test for starch: iodine solution turns from brown to blue-black.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Biuret test
entries: The test for protein: Biuret solution turns from blue to purple.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Emulsion test
entries: The test for lipid: mix with ethanol then water; a milky white emulsion is positive.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
